page: Amazon Web Services m7i.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a custom Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C processor based on the x86_64 architecture operating at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance allocates 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. System memory consists of 16.0 GB of DDR5 RAM clocked at 5 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The processor integrates 105 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for integer and bfloat16 operations.

Performance benchmarks show strong execution on single-threaded tasks. The server achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2025.0 and delivers 32.15 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression, both scoring in the top performance tier. Text processing and single-core stress-ng tests also maintain solid throughput. In contrast, multi-threaded tasks reveal clear scaling constraints due to the 2-core physical limit; compiling software with Clang, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and stress-ng multi-core tests land in the lower quartile. Memory bandwidth measures 25.82 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 27.32 GB/sec for large-block writes, while transactional database and Redis SET operations demonstrate modest throughput.

The m7i.xlarge provision includes no integrated local instance storage and zero GPUs, requiring attached Amazon EBS storage for persistent file systems. Baseline network capacity is configured at 2 Gbps. The instance provides a cost-effective allocation of fourth-generation Intel Xeon features and fast DDR5 memory without overprovisioning execution cores. Its profile is appropriate for general-purpose application hosting, standard web serving, API endpoints, microservices, background job workers, and lightweight prompt processing workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical x86_64 cores paired with 16.0 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 5 GHz. Hardware capabilities include a 105 MB L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix acceleration extensions. It includes no local storage or GPUs, relying on remote EBS volumes and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reveal strong single-thread compute efficiency, ranking high in single-core compression and text processing tests. Multi-core scaling and memory-intensive database throughput remain limited by the dual-core physical topology. The configuration offers balanced resource distribution suitable for running web servers, application runtimes, microservices, and general business software.
